newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lacklustre Australian stocks end just lower.
newsitem.headline: Lacklustre Australian stocks end just lower.

text.p: SPI Futures 2536 -7 US 30yr cl 6.93 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.210 -0.075 Gold NY 349.50 Lon fix 348.90
AUD US$0.7785 (Tue 0.7828) CRB Index cl 251.30 -0.10
*Stocks end just lower in lacklustre trade as market takes breather, little budget impact. Volume 279.62 million, value A$595.45 million, 1,086 stocks traded, 348 steady, 357 up, 381 down.
The Australian share market ended just lower on Wednesday after a day of lacklustre trade with little impact from Tuesday's Federal government budget.
The All Ordinaries index lost 3.9 points to 2,530.4.
The June share price index futures were seven points lower at 2,536, a 5.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Volume failed to top even the A$600 million mark.
Brokers said the market had seen moderate two-way business with little specific to be gleaned for the broader equity market from the 1997/98 fiscal programme.
"I don't think our market has drawn very much from the budget," said Derek Bond, director at Brisbane-based brokerage, Burrell and Co.
"It's been a fairly lacklustre day in all. The market is just going about its business. The main focus in the market was the Westpac result."
Westpac Banking Corporation did indeed feature, as did its other "big four" colleagues, Commonwealth Bank, National Australia Bank and ANZ Bank in a day of choppy, volatile trade for the sector.

NAB, Commonwealth Bank bounced off intraday lows to streak to record highs of A$18.49 and A$14.82 respectively, after Westpac posted a better-than-expected 12.9 percent rise in first half net profit to A$638 million.

Those pricing levels looked expensive for many though, and sellers quickly took the opportunity to cash in. NAB shares ended just up 0.003 at A$18.34, while Commonwealth Bank held most gains to close 23 cents higher at A$14.78.
Westpac shares jumped 10 cents an intraday high of A$7.60 after the result, but by the end of the day were down five cents at A$7.45 as traders decided better value lay elsewhere.
Media giant News Corp lost most ground among the large capitalisation stocks.

Its shares dived over 3.5 percent to A$5.72 with traders unhappy about talk of further acquisitions. Featuring was the the long-rumoured US$1 billion deal with U.S.-based International Family Entertainment and talk of New's FoxSports division buying the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball franchise for over US$350 million.
Miner CRA was the pick among the leaders, up two to A$19.82 after its dual listed sibling RTZ Plc hit a 12 month high in London trading.

Gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd made back some of its recent substantial losses, jumping nine percent to an intraday high of A$3.52 after managing director John Quinn resigned. The stock later eased to end up 25 cents at A$3.46.
"Newcrest was the star performer in the gold sector. The market took the change of management in its stride," Bond said.

Shares in investment house Macquarie Bank dived nearly three percent to an intraday low of A$9.28 amid fears a budget crackdown on trade in dividend franking credits would harm its equities business. The shares recovered some ground in the afternoon to close 10 cents lower at A$9.44.
Falls slightly outnumbered rises, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures volumes were strong as traders reset positions in a choppy day's trade but options activity matched the underlying markets with a very slow day.
Total options traded 21,592 (30,774)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 7,601 (5,926)

In other local markets, Australian bond yields remained close to the day's highs in the wake of the budget and ahead of the May 20 FOMC. By 4.55 p.m. (0655 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.77 percent, up from Tuesday's 7.69 percent.
The Australian dollar settled into all too familiar range trading as dealers put the disappointment of the budget behind them only to find fundamentals offered little direction either.
By 4.55 p.m. (0655 GMT), the dollar had ventured to US$0.7776/81 up on an early US$0.7760 support but well short of the US$0.7826/31 level enjoyed before the budget's release.
